When the car starts and the phone is not linked over Bluetooth yet, MG4Link calls it after this delay. 15 s leaves the car time to reconnect it by itself; if your car never does, a shorter delay connects sooner.
Fine-tuning and diagnostics. The defaults suit most cars.
Before starting Android Auto, waits up to 5 s for the car to finish connecting the phone over Bluetooth, so music that starts by itself plays in the car instead of on the phone\'s speaker.
Give the Android Auto dongle priority at start-up

Experimental, for a wireless Android Auto adapter (dongle) only. At start-up the car waits (time set below) before connecting the phone over Bluetooth, so the adapter reaches it first. Leave it off without an adapter.
How long the car waits for Android Auto through the dongle before connecting the phone over Bluetooth as usual. Only with the option above.
Experimental. Keeps the car\'s Wi-Fi connected for internet during wireless Android Auto, when its network allows it.

When the car is connected to a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network on channel 36 to 48 (a home box, for example), it stays connected for internet and the wireless Android Auto hotspot opens on the same channel. The car's single Wi-Fi radio then never has to switch channels, which is what causes short stutters. MG4Link remembers that channel, so the next hotspot opens on it straight away.

If you switch the car's Wi-Fi on during a drive, it has 30 s to join a known network. Android Auto may be interrupted for a few seconds while it looks, and for about 15 s if the hotspot has to move to the network's channel.

On another channel, on 2.4 GHz, or as soon as the car loses the network while driving, the car's Wi-Fi goes off as usual. Android Auto may have a little less bandwidth while both share the channel.

If you notice other instabilities than those described above (during the connection), please report them on GitHub with a log.
